messages:
maya: Heads up — spotted a ~90s burst of corrected ECC flips on scratch NVMe pool eu-west4 that triggered janitor evicts and blocked ~12 GPU attaches. Logs attached below.
raj: ugh. any drive IDs or SMART spikes?
maya: excerpt from dmesg:
```
[1758883123.123456] nvme0: corrected ECC errors: 324 flips in 2m
[1758883124.223456] nvme0: device reset due to health deterioration
[1758883125.323456] janitor: evicting /scratch/node-gg/ephemeral-1234 (score 87)
```
most flips on nvme0 and nvme2 across the same rack. SMART shows rising volatile_count.
leo: observed similar pattern last month but not this clustered. Could be thermal + firmware corner case. Any recent kernel or fw pushes to that AZ?
maya: we pushed nvme-fw 2.1.9 -> 2.1.10 to eu-west4 3h earlier (rolling). rollouts showed low failure rate but this looks correlated by rack id.
infra-bot: [ALERT] rolling-update: nvme-fw v2.1.10 completed on 18 hosts in eu-west4 at 1758879000. CI: canary passed.
noa: repro idea: janitor aggressive eviction + sustained write streams -> IO amplification -> temp thermal spike -> ECC flips. Need to confirm if janitor sweep cadence caused synchronous fsync storms.
raj: mitigation for now? pinning? can we fallback those hosts to older FW quickly or throttle janitor?
leo: immediate options: 1) pause janitor on affected nodes (`/srv/ops/bin/janitor pause --node node-gg*`) 2) set nvme write cache off (temporary perf hit) 3) throttle attach scheduling to avoid new GPU attaches to those hosts. I recommend pausing janitor & throttling attaches.
maya: doing pause now on the 18 hosts. running: `/srv/ops/bin/janitor pause --selector rack=eu-west4-rack7` (kicked off)
maya: also set attach throttle rule: `policy.attach_throttle.add --match eu-west4-rack7 --reason "nvme-ecc-burst" --max 1m`
raj: good. can infra-bot surface which GPU requests were pending? I want to requeue non-critical ones.
infra-bot: query: pending attaches in eu-west4-rack7 = 9 (6 preemptible, 3 reserved). Holding preemptible ones.
noa: FYI: if firmware is the culprit, fallback is risky mid-day. prefer throttling + thermal cooldown and extended scrub. Also collect full SMART dumps and nvme-cli error logs for vendor support.
leo: agree. can we enable vendor diag logging and hit support? I can open a ticket if we get dumps.
maya: collected nvme-cli `error-log` and `smart-log` for nvme0,nvme2. files: /tmp/nvme-dumps/eu-west4-rack7-2026-03-21.tar.gz
raj: ETA for janitor resume?
maya: will resume after 30m cooldown + verify SMART counters stable. posting progress every 5m.
noa: also add a temporary rule to reduce janitor concurrency globally in eu-west4 to avoid wave effects: `janitor.config.set --region eu-west4 --concurrency 2`
leo: sounds good. Please keep live notes here. If SMART still rising after cooldown, we should consider targeted firmware rollback and vendor escalation.
maya: update @5m: SMART delta per-disk dropped from +120 flips -> +8 flips in last 5m after pause + throttle. attaching logs to ticket if needed.
raj: nice. tagging infra-ops-runbook: `storage/ecc-flip-burst` so we can run postmortem checklist.
infra-bot: ticket created: INC-9987 "eu-west4 rack7 nvme corrected-ecc burst" assigned to leo, priority P2.
leo: I'll open vendor support and include /tmp tarball. thanks for fast mitigation.
maya: thanks team. will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
